Identity.History: The Zapotecs developed one of Mesoamerica’s earliest great civilizations in the valleys of Oaxaca. By the first millennium BC they had built major urban centers, especially Monte Albán, with temples, tombs, plazas, and carved monuments. Zapotec rulers controlled surrounding communities through warfare, tribute, and alliances while developing writing and calendars. Their political dominance later declined, but Zapotec culture endured for centuries.
